tracks.title: Core Python
tracks.summary: The object model, the built-in containers, functions and scope, your own types, and the cost of the code you just wrote.
tracks.goal: Read an unfamiliar Python traceback and name the cause; choose the container that makes an operation O(1) instead of O(n); write functions, closures, decorators and classes whose failure modes you can predict before running them.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.summary: Names are bindings, not boxes. Everything downstream — aliasing bugs, mutable defaults, dict keys — falls out of that one fact.

modules.title: Functions and Scope
modules.summary: Signatures are an API contract. Closures are how Python remembers, and late binding is how it surprises you.

modules.title: Data Modelling
modules.summary: Build collections declaratively, then build your own types that behave like the built-in ones.

modules.title: Correctness and Performance
modules.summary: Errors are part of your API, and so is the complexity of the loop you just wrote. This is where the project lives.

skills.title: Predict the effect of a mutation through an alias
skills.description: Given two names bound to the same object, say what a mutation through one does to the other, and distinguish rebinding from mutating.

skills.title: Write conditionals that do not confuse empty with missing
skills.description: Use `is None` where absence is meant, truth testing where emptiness is meant, and know which one a caller will trip over.

skills.title: Choose the container the workload actually needs
skills.description: Pick list, tuple, dict, set or deque from the operations the code performs, not from habit, and justify it in complexity terms.

skills.title: State the time and space cost of a piece of Python
skills.description: Read a function and name its asymptotic cost, including the costs hidden inside built-in operations, then fix the term that dominates.

skills.title: Express a transformation as a comprehension
skills.description: Convert an accumulator loop into a list, dict, set or generator expression, and know when not to.

skills.title: Design a function signature a caller cannot misuse
skills.description: Order positional, keyword-only and variadic parameters so the common call is short and the wrong call is impossible.

skills.title: Keep per-call state out of default arguments
skills.description: Recognise a default evaluated once at definition time, and rewrite it so each call gets its own object.

skills.title: Say what a closure captured and when it was read
skills.description: Distinguish capturing a variable from capturing its value, and predict what a closure created in a loop will see.

skills.title: Write a decorator that preserves its wrapped function
skills.description: Build a parameterised decorator that keeps the name, docstring and signature metadata of what it wraps and does not swallow exceptions.

skills.title: Implement the dunder protocols a type claims to support
skills.description: Give a type equality, hashing, ordering, iteration and a useful repr that agree with each other and with the language's own rules.

skills.title: Define what a function raises and why
skills.description: Choose or define the exception type, decide between EAFP and LBYL, and chain causes so the original failure is not lost.

skills.title: Go from a traceback to the line that is actually wrong
skills.description: Read a traceback bottom-up, separate the raising frame from the offending frame, and use the exception type to narrow the cause before touching the code.
